name: European summer heat waves (2022)
headline: Europe's hottest summer on record at the time brought repeated heat waves from Spain to the UK. An epidemiological study of 35 countries attributed about 61,700 deaths to the heat.
numbers: High: systematic count or epidemiological estimate
timeline: Early heat waves in Spain and France.
Extreme heat reaches north-west Europe; the UK records 40 °C for the first time (19 July).
Drought and heat across much of the continent.
Ballester et al. (Nature Medicine) estimate 61,672 heat-related deaths.

The weather setup: Summer 2022 was Europe's hottest on record at the time, with repeated heat waves from June to August and widespread drought. The UK passed 40 °C for the first time on 19 July.
What made it so deadly: As in 2003, the dead were overwhelmingly elderly. The study found heat-related mortality 56% higher among women than men relative to population. Despite the heat-health plans introduced after 2003, the toll remained very high, which the authors say should prompt a re-evaluation of prevention and adaptation.
The death toll and how it was measured: Ballester et al. (2023) used 45 million death records from Eurostat for 35 countries and an epidemiological model of the temperature–mortality relationship to estimate 61,672 heat-related deaths between 30 May and 4 September 2022: Italy 18,010, Spain 11,324, Germany 8,173, France 4,807, the UK 3,469 and Greece 3,092. Because it models temperature-attributable deaths rather than all excess deaths, it is not directly comparable with the 2003 figure, but it is among the best-quantified tolls here.

sources.title: Ballester, J. et al. (2023). Heat-related mortality in Europe during the summer of 2022. Nature Medicine 29: 1857–1866.
ISGlobal: Record-breaking heat in the summer of 2022 caused more than 61,000 deaths in Europe
